exposure: Ponseti technique for congenital talipes equinovarus management
Mode of birth (Lower Segment Cesarean Section - LSCS)
outcome: Number of casts required for correction
Characteristics of clubfoot incidence (sex predominance, bilateral involvement, first-born representation, positive family history, parental consanguinity, LSCS delivery)
cohort: The study cohort consists of 30 children diagnosed with congenital clubfoot who were consulted at Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Warangal, India.
finding: The Ponseti method proved to be an effective, non-invasive approach for managing congenital clubfoot, ensuring high rates of correction and low recurrence when initiated early.
mod_finding: 100% of patients were delivered via lower segment cesarean section (LSCS), which was noted as a potential contributing factor to clubfoot incidence.
